scope: Tip UITextViewer line breaking, row and scroll contract; source-only

tip_creation.sendmsg: Heading and each tip string are sent as message=29, val2=38, val3=0.

ascii_breaking.finding: Base CLanguage::GetWordBreak ignores size and returns CharNextExA(g_codePage,text,0); for ASCII that advances one byte. CutStringWithColor scans in those codepage steps, remembers the latest space boundary, skips repeated spaces while updating that boundary, and when the 38-step limit is reached wraps at that remembered boundary; if no space is available it hard-splits at the current step. Thus it is codepage-aware character stepping plus space-preferred wrapping, not a dictionary word-break routine.
ascii_breaking.markers: A ^ followed by six valid hex digits is preserved in output but advances the wrap limit by 7, so it does not count toward the 38 visible steps.

blank_and_newline.empty: An empty input string produces no output line in CutStringWithColor; UITextViewer consequently calls AddItem zero times. A blank Tip entry therefore does not occupy a visible row. Nonempty whitespace input follows the ordinary wrapping path.
blank_and_newline.lf: Tip loading splits LF into individual strings before viewer calls. CutStringWithColor itself does not special-case LF. Its CR branch only runs when readCR is true; the Tip viewer passes val3=0/readCR=false, so CR is not removed by this wrapper. The Tip parser does not strip CR; subsequent rendering of an embedded CR is not established here.

color.finding: Recognized ^ + six-hex color markers remain in each output substring. UITextViewer::OnDraw initializes colorRef to zero, scans every preceding item when vertically scrolled using FindColorMark/InterpretColor, then passes the same colorRef through visible items via TextOutWithDecoration. This carries color state across wrapped rows and across the heading/tip list items; wrapping does not synthesize a repeated color marker.

viewer_rows_and_scroll.defaults: UITextViewer constructor sets m_itemSpacing=18 and m_noColor=0. It is a UIListBox; vertical scrollbar is enabled when stored item count exceeds floor(h/18), here 7. Each wrapped output line is one stored item/row.
viewer_rows_and_scroll.page: UIListBox message 9 moves vertical offset up by h/itemSpacing - 1; message 10 moves it down by the same amount. Here this is 6 rows (one row overlap), clamped to 0..itemCount-7. Message 7 moves by the supplied val1 line count.
viewer_rows_and_scroll.scrollbar: UIListBox::OnCreate creates a 13-pixel scrollbar child; RecalcScrbarPos sets its max/current range from itemCount and visible row count. Horizontal scrollbar remains disabled in the default listbox state for this viewer.

separate_cases.multilingual: The base and Thai GetWordBreak implementations both call CharNextExA(g_codePage,...); other language subclasses were not audited. CutStringWithColor has a separate g_multiLang/non-ASCII path that inserts a 3-byte charset marker into subsequent wrapped output rows. Do not reduce this to ASCII byte counts.
separate_cases.item_markup: CutStringWithColor also detects valid item indicators via IsValidItemIndicator and may emit a separate item display-name string; this branch is excluded from the plain ASCII text contract.
separate_cases.limits: No rendering claim is made for retained CR bytes, invalid color escapes, item-indicator markup, or other language subclasses.
